rules.statement: Resolve a principal from a presented token (such as a token exchange `subject_token`) only from its subject claim; never fall back to its `client_id` claim, and reserve client-as-principal resolution for paths where the authenticated caller is that client acting for itself.
rules.why: A `client_id` claim in a presented token comes from the token, not from the authenticated caller, so falling back to it lets a token's audience or an external issuer impersonate a client's principal as a user subject.
rules.check: Look for a shared principal resolver that falls back to `client_id` when `sub` is missing, and check whether token exchange or other grant handlers call it on a presented token instead of answering `invalid_grant`.

rules.statement: When several endpoints need the same authorization or refusal check, put the check and its error result into one shared step (a helper returning `IResult?` or an endpoint filter) instead of pasting the block into each handler.
rules.why: An endpoint added or changed later can leave out a pasted guard, which opens a privilege gap, and the copies drift apart.
rules.check: Look for the same `if (!await ...) return Forbidden/AuthorizationFailed(...)` block, or the same lookup feeding it, repeated across handlers of one route group.

rules.statement: Reuse the existing entity-to-resource mapper and shared listing helpers instead of copying them into a new endpoint handler.
rules.why: Copied mappers and loops drift apart when a resource gains a field or a fix lands in one copy only.
rules.check: Look for new `To...Resource` methods or listing loops that duplicate ones already in sibling handlers.

rules.statement: Don't fetch entities one store call per id inside a loop; add or use a batched get-many store method that reads them in one query.
rules.why: A per-id loop costs one database round trip per entity on every request.
rules.check: Look for `await store.GetOrDefaultAsync(id)` or similar inside a `foreach` over ids.

rules.statement: Give new private helper methods `///` XML doc summaries, with `<returns>` saying what a bool result means, not just a `//` comment.
rules.why: Without it the meaning of the return value (for example, true means the caller may act) is undocumented.
rules.check: Look for new private methods, especially ones returning bool, that have no `/// <summary>`.

rules.statement: Don't report an endpoint that opens its ambient tenant scope by hand when its route has no tenant id parameter for the shared route-group tenant filter to read and sibling code opens a fixed tenant scope the same way.
rules.why: The shared filter scopes a route by its `{tenantId}` segment and has nothing to read on routes that name no tenant.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the route template has a tenant id segment and how sibling authorization code opens the same fixed scope.

rules.statement: Don't flag case-insensitive deduplication or comparison of identifiers as a bug when the stores key those identifiers by a normalized form and match them case-insensitively.
rules.why: Ids differing only by case name the same entity, so case-insensitive dedup is correct and an ordinal sort only makes order stable.
rules.check: Before reporting a comparer mismatch, check how the store keys and normalizes the identifier.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a new index for an unbounded predicate on a rarely run operation such as a delete when sibling stores already use the same pattern under a recorded decision.
rules.why: An index is warranted only when that operation at scale needs it.
rules.check: Before reporting, check how often the operation runs and whether sibling stores use the same predicate.

rules.statement: Don't ask for Storybook stories for an app-local frontend component; stories cover the shared `packages/*` components, and app components are covered by their tests.
rules.why: The convention scopes Storybook to shared package components.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing story, check whether the component lives under a shared package or inside an app.
